title: Transcutaneous Tumor Photolabeling to Track Immune Cells in Kaede Mice
author: Dean, Kennedy, et al.
materials: LIVE/DEAD Fixable Near-IR Dead Cell Stain Kit

steps.title: Culture tumor cells to confluency
steps.instruction: Grow MC38 cells in RPMI‑based medium and E0771 cells in DMEM at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ in T75 flasks until they reach approximately 70–80 % confluency.

steps.title: Pre‑warm reagents
steps.instruction: Warm the appropriate culture medium to 37 °C and bring TrypLE Express and PBS to room temperature (≈20–25 °C).

steps.title: Wash cells with PBS
steps.instruction: Aspirate the spent culture medium from the flasks and gently rinse the adherent cells with PBS.

steps.title: Detach cells with TrypLE
steps.instruction: Add 3 mL TrypLE Express to each flask, return the flask to the incubator for 2–3 min, then check for cell detachment and gently shake the flask if required. (CRITICAL: Optimize digestion time for each trypsin‑like reagent to avoid affecting viability.)

steps.title: Neutralize and collect cells
steps.instruction: Add 7 mL pre‑warmed culture medium to each flask, gently resuspend the cells, and transfer the suspension to a 50 mL centrifuge tube.

steps.title: Centrifuge cell suspension
steps.instruction: Spin the tubes at 300–400 × g for 5 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Wash and count cells
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 10 mL PBS, withdraw 10 µL for cell counting with a hemocytometer, then centrifuge again at 300–400 × g for 5 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Adjust cell concentration
steps.instruction: Resuspend the cells in PBS to obtain 2.5 × 10⁶ cells/mL for MC38 or 5 × 10⁶ cells/mL for E0771.

steps.title: Aliquot cells for injection
steps.instruction: Transfer 1 mL of the appropriately concentrated cell suspension into 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes, keep on ice, and inject into mice within 1 hour to maintain viability.

steps.title: Plate samples for flow cytometry
steps.instruction: Place each cell sample into a well of a 96‑well plate, centrifuge at 400 × g for 3 min, then discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Fc block incubation
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL FACS buffer containing anti‑CD16/32 Fc‑blocking antibodies to each well and incubate 20 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Wash after Fc block
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 400 × g for 3 min, discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Stain cells with antibodies
steps.instruction: Resuspend each cell pellet in 100 µL of the prepared antibody mix and incubate 30 min at 4 °C. Include single‑color controls for each fluorophore as well as Kaede‑green and Kaede‑red controls (Kaede‑red can be generated by photoconverting splenocytes with the Dymax BlueWave QX4 system).

steps.title: Wash post‑staining
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 400 × g for 3 min, discard supernatant, wash cells once with PBS, then centrifuge again at 400 × g for 3 min.

steps.title: Viability dye incubation
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 100 µL PBS containing LIVE/DEAD viability dye and incubate 15 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Final wash before fixation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 400 × g for 3 min and discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Fix cells (pause point)
steps.instruction: Resuspend fully stained cells in 100 µL BD Cytofix, incubate 30 min at 4 °C, then store at 4 °C in foil‑wrapped, dark containers for up to 2–3 days. (Optional: permeabilize with BD Cytoperm or Foxp3 transcription‑factor buffer for intracellular staining, following the manufacturer’s instructions.)

steps.title: Acquire data on cytometer
steps.instruction: Resuspend cells in 300 µL FACS buffer, add counting beads if required, and run the samples on a flow cytometer.

description: This protocol describes the establishment of subcutaneous (s.c.) tumors using the colorectal cell line MC38, and orthotopic breast tumors using E0771 cells. Both subcutaneous and mammary fat pad (m.f.p) tumors provide an easily accessible tumor that can be readily exposed transcutaneously to the near-UV light required for Kaede photoconversion. Whilst in this paper we describe two cell lines, in practice this approach is applicable to any non-pigmented tumor cell lines. The main limitation of photoconversion is light penetration, therefore tumor size, pigmentation (such as melanin produced by B16F10 melanoma cells), and depth of tumor implantation must be considered when attempting transcutaneous photolabeling. This protocol can be divided into three sections: culture and inoculation of tumor cells, Kaede photoconversion using near-UV light, and the isolation and acquisition of intratumoral cells.
